title: RemoteFunction
summary: Client ↔ server request/response: InvokeServer yields until the server's OnServerInvoke returns a value. Use sparingly — it blocks the calling thread and is deadlock-prone.

methods.name: InvokeServer
methods.description: Client only. Yields the calling thread until the server's OnServerInvoke handler returns. Returns whatever the handler returned.

methods.name: InvokeClient
methods.description: Server only. Yields until the target client's OnClientInvoke returns. Optional timeout (errors when exceeded). Never trust what comes back.

properties.name: OnServerInvoke
properties.description: Server-assigned callback: `remote.OnServerInvoke = function(player, ...) return value end`. Assigned, not connected. If unset when a client invokes, the client errors.

properties.name: OnClientInvoke
properties.description: Client-assigned callback for server→client invokes. Set this before the server might invoke, or the server call fails/times out.

details.heading: Yielding semantics
details.body: InvokeServer blocks the calling thread (not the whole game) until the server responds. If the server handler itself yields (task.wait, DataStore call), the client waits for all of it.

details.heading: Error propagation
details.body: If the OnServerInvoke handler errors, the error propagates to the invoking client thread — wrap in pcall if the server handler can fail.

details.heading: Deadlocks
details.body: If the client invokes the server and the server's handler invokes that same client back (or vice versa), both sides wait forever. Keep invokes one-directional per call chain.

explanation.whatItIs: The question-and-answer remote. The client asks 'what's my save data?' and *waits* for the answer, like a function call that crosses the network.
explanation.whyItExists: Sometimes the client genuinely needs data only the server has, right now: prices, permissions, generated level layout. RemoteEvent can't return values; RemoteFunction can.
whenToUse: Fetching server-authoritative data on demand (shop prices, inventory snapshot)
Occasional requests where waiting is acceptable and expected
Server asking ONE client a question it must answer (rare; always use a timeout with InvokeClient)
whenNotToUse: High-frequency communication — every invoke yields a thread and waits a round trip; use RemoteEvent/UnreliableRemoteEvent
Push-style updates ('tell me when X changes') — that's event-shaped: RemoteEvent
Anything security-critical based on the client's ANSWER — a client can return garbage or never respond; validate or don't depend on it
Chained invokes (server handler invokes back) — deadlock risk
explanation.mentalModel:
```text
CLIENT                                SERVER
  │  InvokeServer("price", "Sword")     │
  ├─────────────────────────────────────▶│  OnServerInvoke(player, ...)
  │          (yielded, waiting…)        │     return 250
  │◀─────────────────────────────────────┤
  │  local price = 250  (resumes)       │
```
Like calling a function whose body runs on another machine.
tips: Default to RemoteEvent; reach for RemoteFunction only when you truly need a return value
pcall InvokeServer if the handler could error or you want timeouts handled gracefully
For 'server asks client', always pass a timeout to InvokeClient and treat timeout as refusal
Cache responses client-side when the data rarely changes
commonMistakes: Invoking before the server has ASSIGNED OnServerInvoke — the invoke errors ('Server has not set OnServerInvoke')
Using invokes in RenderStepped/Heartbeat loops — yields wreck your framerate
Trusting InvokeClient results for authoritative decisions
Deadlocking by invoking back into the thread that's waiting on you

examples.title: Client asks for the shop price
examples.code:
-- == Script (server) — set up the answerer ONCE at startup ==
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local getPrice = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetPrice")
local PRICES = { Sword = 250, Shield = 100 }

getPrice.OnServerInvoke = function(player, itemName)
    if typeof(itemName) ~= "string" then
        return nil
    end
    return PRICES[itemName]
end

-- == LocalScript (client) ==
local getPrice = ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("GetPrice")

local ok, price = pcall(function()
    return getPrice:InvokeServer("Sword")
end)

if ok and price then
    print("Sword costs", price)   --> Sword costs 250
else
    warn("Price lookup failed")
end
examples.whyItWorks: The server assigns OnServerInvoke once; each client invoke runs that function with `player` first (same rule as OnServerEvent) and returns the value across the network.
examples.commonMistake: Forgetting the server-side assignment (or assigning it AFTER clients start invoking) — invokes then error on the client.

examples.title: Server → client invoke with timeout
examples.code:
-- Server asks ONE client a question, but never hangs on it:
local ok, answer = pcall(function()
    return remote:InvokeClient(player, 5, "Do you accept the trade?")  -- 5s timeout
end)

if ok and answer == true then
    print(player.Name .. " accepted")
else
    print(player.Name .. " did not answer (or said no)")
end
examples.commonMistake: InvokeClient without a timeout: if the client's OnClientInvoke isn't set (or the client is malicious), the server thread can wait indefinitely.
